scope: Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Chapter 4 (with Online Appendix A2): Debt, deficits, discount rates and inflation. Innovations, martingale-difference shocks and moving-average representations; the linearised flow and present-value identities, derived as exact derivatives; unexpected inflation equals minus a(rho) times the surplus shock, with the AR(1), MA(1), ARMA and permanent-transitory cases; the surplus-process facts and debt feedback; the generalised decompositions (4.11)-(4.13) with Campbell-Shiller and Campbell-Ammer; VAR identities, Cholesky ordering and the present-value tautology; conditioning down; invertibility and Hilbert-space Wold statements; Hansen-Sargent. Data, estimates and figures are out of scope. Printed errors corrected with Lean counterexamples. Genuine probability models: a measure-theoretic expectation system (Mathlib conditional expectation on a filtered probability space, bounded measurable processes, almost-sure statements, bridges both ways to the core finite-tree systems, a genuine i.i.d. infinite-product economy that is not finitely supported) and the chapter's stochastic results re-proved there.
source: John H. Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Princeton University Press, Chapter 4, pp. 81-116, and Online Appendix A2, pp. 593-611.
